name: Back to Basics 1
source: written 27 Aug 2026 as the program a new person gets before anything is known about them. Built from the fundamentals list in the exercise database, bodyweight first, nothing that needs a gym.
entryIf: Start here unless you can already do 3 × 10 bodyweight squats and 3 × 8 push-ups from the floor with good shape.

methods.name: Straight sets
methods.what: Sets and reps, one movement at a time, generous rest.
methods.why: Level 1 has exactly one variable and it is the movement itself. Everything else - tempo, the clock, failure - waits until the shape is owned.

arc.rule: Every set stops two reps before it gets hard. This week is about where your body goes, not what it can do.
Same numbers as week 1. Slower down, full range, no bouncing. If week 1 felt easy this is where it starts to bite.
Add a set to the first work block of each day. Everything else stays.
Squat, push and hinge get one honest hard set. That number is where the next program starts.

constraints.unknown: nothing is known about this person yet - so nothing here loads a spine heavily, nothing jumps, and every movement has an easier version one tap away
constraints.time: 30 minutes, three days. A fourth day is a decision for week five, not week one.

goals: Learn the six shapes everything else is built from
Turn up three times a week for four weeks
Finish week 4 with a number on the squat, the push and the hinge
Leave knowing which movements you want more of

d1.name: Squat & Push
d1.why: The two shapes you use most and think about least - standing up out of a chair, and pushing a door. Everything is done where you can already do it well; the point of week one is a rep you would be happy to show someone.

blocks.name: Loosen off
blocks.note: Straight through, no rest. Two rounds if you have time.

items.note: Slow. Breathe out as you round.
Knee travels over the toes, heel stays down.
Sit into the bottom of a squat and rock. If you cannot get down, hold a doorframe.

blocks.name: A · Bodyweight Squat
blocks.note: 3 × 10, rest 60s. Sit back like there is a chair behind you. Stop the set the moment the knees fall inward.

items.note: 60s rest · hold a doorframe if balance is the problem

blocks.name: B · Incline Push-Up
blocks.note: 3 × 8, rest 60s. Hands on a counter or a wall. Higher hands is easier - start easier than you think.

items.note: 60s rest · body in one line from ear to heel

blocks.name: C · Glute Bridge
blocks.note: 3 × 12, rest 45s. The one that makes the squat better.

items.note: 45s rest · squeeze at the top, ribs down

blocks.name: Middle
blocks.note: Straight through, 45s between rounds. Two rounds.

items.note: Stop when the hips drop, not at the time.
Lower back stays flat on the floor the whole time.

d2.name: Hinge & Pull
d2.why: Picking something up, and pulling something towards you. The hinge is the one people get wrong and the one that protects a back, so it gets the most attention and the strictest stop rule.

items.note: Arms straight, squeeze the shoulder blades.
Slow. Nothing else moves.

blocks.name: A · Romanian Deadlift
blocks.note: 3 × 10, rest 75s. Push the hips back, not down. The set ends the rep your back changes shape.

items.note: 75s rest · light. Weight is not the point in week one.

blocks.name: B · Incline Row
blocks.note: 3 × 8, rest 60s. Under a bar or a table, feet forward. The higher the bar, the easier it is.

items.note: 60s rest · chest to the bar, elbows past the ribs

blocks.name: C · Farmer's Carry
blocks.note: 3 rounds of 30 seconds, rest 45s. Heavy enough that the last ten seconds are honest.

items.note: 45s rest · tall, shoulders down, do not lean
Knees down is a real option.
Feet on the floor taking some weight is fine.

d3.name: Full Body
d3.why: The same six shapes, loaded a little differently, so week one has repetition without being the same session three times. This is the day where you find out which movements you actually like.

items.note: Waking them up, not training them.

blocks.name: A · Goblet Squat
blocks.note: 3 × 10, rest 75s. Holding a weight at the chest makes the squat easier to do well, not harder.

items.note: 75s rest · elbows inside the knees at the bottom

blocks.name: B · Knee Push-Up
blocks.note: 3 × 10, rest 60s. Knees down on purpose - it lets you do more good reps than a hard version does.

items.note: 60s rest · hips in line with the shoulders, not up

blocks.name: C · Single-Leg Bridge
blocks.note: 3 × 8 each side, rest 45s. One leg finds the side that is asleep.

items.note: 45s rest · hips stay level
Knees bent and hands by the hips is the starting version.
One weight. Do not let the ribs tip.
